answer: Each identity claims one vertex in a nebula graph and posts a 70-credit bond keyed to its cipher key. It forwards a cipher-sealed packet on a vertex-disjoint route, filing its hop list. An auditor replays the seal against the nebula graph table and burns the bond for a reused vertex, broken seal, or skipped hop. First route costs 36; k-th 36+6(k-1), each taken vertex forcing a priced detour; 1000th 6030, 1000 fakes 3,033,000 plus 70,000 bonds. An honest agent pays once, then redeems its bond. A rented-vertex ring fails: its vertex carries another identity's cipher seal, exposed on replay.
